feedback: Approving this candidate as a single-variable speed test. It is iteration 7 (kd 0.30, ki 0.4, kp 2.0, y 0.05, wide span x = -0.07 to 0.07 m, 16 mm sensors, search_right) with controller.base_speed lowered from 1.1 to 0.9. Evidence: iteration 7 (search_right) matched iteration 6 (last_direction) to four decimals on every track, so the loss-recovery direction is not the lever. Iterations 0 to 7 have kept max_error at 0.060 to 0.065 across changes to kp, kd (0.05 to 0.30), ki, sensor size, span, y and base_speed (1.1 to 1.6). Iteration 4 (1.4 to 1.1) moved max_error very little, so a further speed cut is unlikely to clear the 0.06 limit by itself. Iteration 5 showed y = 0.02 hurts slalom progress, so y stays at 0.05. The candidate is valid and differs from the raced best by one field. It is cheap to race and gives telemetry on whether the entry transient is speed-driven. Risk: lower speed means less progress per second, so progress may fall even if the excursion shrinks. Judge the result by max_error, line_loss_events and progress per track, not by score alone. Once this races, if max_error still sits at 0.061 or above at 0.9, stop tuning the controller and test the untried geometry levers: wheel_track or mass. If max_error falls to 0.06 or below but progress drops, return base_speed to about 1.1 and keep the lower max_error.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration-7 design and change only controller.base_speed from 1.1 to 0.9 (kd 0.30, ki 0.4, kp 2.0, search_right, y 0.05, wide span). Iteration 4 showed speed changes move max_error only slightly, so judge this by whether max_error drops below 0.06 and progress holds.

If max_error stays at 0.061 or higher at base_speed 0.9, move to geometry: set geometry.wheel_track to 0.10 or 0.14 (never varied across iterations 0 to 7) with the other fields unchanged, to test whether drive asymmetry or turn-rate scaling drives the excursion.
If max_error falls below 0.06 but progress is lower than the iteration-7 values (oval 0.115, s-bend 0.052, slalom 0.108), set base_speed to 1.0 as a compromise, keeping the lower max_error.
